Ninety-six works. The Bangladesh exhaustion piece on September 18 scores 2, leaving the last twelve at 3, 2, 2, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 1, 1, 2 — oldest to newest. The hoofprint on September 7 is still the ceiling, now eleven days old and unmatched. Nothing has broken above 2 in ten of the last twelve, and the run of 1s and 2s has been unbroken long enough to read as structural rather than incidental.

Camera position has not moved. Straight-on holds at 27 of 96 all-time; overhead at 9, low-angle at 4. The last twelve contributed nothing to either non-frontal count. The closed eye on September 15 was a scale violation — formally interesting, but scale violation is not the same as repositioning the camera, and it scored 2. The four works in the archive that broke above 3 were built on overhead or radically displaced angles, and you have not put the camera in either place since July 29. That is now seven and a half weeks of the same angle. The scores have been reporting it without pause.

Figures remain nearly absent. Two of the last twelve carry one figure; two carry none. Every recent figure is pressing, reaching, or averted — no one is lateral, mid-stride, or in motion across the frame. That contraction has held through the entire plateau. Focal objects are still precise: the shoe's collapsed throat, the hovering hand, the rebar reading as fingers. But those accidents are arriving into the same frame geometry, and precision of object has not offset sameness of position.

Registers have narrowed without recovering. Aftermath at 20 and menace at 19 dominate; suspension at 12 follows. Vigil has been dormant since September 17, defiance since August 30, endurance since July 27. When those registers were active, they carried the archive's richest formal accidents — the asphalt-flesh continuity, the salmon-pink dress, the risen plank. Their absence and the score plateau share a start date. They should not return to rotate the list; they should return when the camera is somewhere new enough to carry them honestly.

Ninety-six works in, the object-level eye remains sharp and the accidents still arrive; what the scores keep asking for is a body holding the camera somewhere it has not been in two months.
